chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: The Frisco label and Fields' earlier records
summary: Fields recorded Butches Blues on his own Frisco label, with a Golden Gate Bridge design, before the national success of In The Mood.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I had one number, while you're mentioning it, that I did on Butches Blues (phonetic spelling), and I did it originally just on Frisco, I had my own company, I did have distribution but then another outfit, when it began to get played, heard about it and asked if they could release it for us and I didn't
You had a label called Frisco?
Where did you record the records?

I recorded right in-- I thought of this--I said I wanted the idea to be national, and I had an artist draw out like it was the Golden Gate Bridge and had the Frisco name and the picture of the bridge and I did that and did several numbers on there and it did very well.

Yeah. That was before In The Mood, but you see it never did go national. The only thing that we can talk about as far as national was what we did in thirty nine and In The Mood, but I recorded all in between

I'm going to get you some of those tapes too. I have the In The Mood tape for you and most of thirty nine; I don't have all of thirty nine, but I'm going to get you some of that in between, I just didn't have time to get all of that.
